passage: Chidi looked up from the loading schedule and saw Paulo standing very still by the printer, his face gone the colour of the paper in his hand. The sheets were rattling slightly. "You okay?" Chidi asked. Paulo gave a thin smile and said, "Fine, just a bit warm." But he didn't move. Chidi thought of the shouting match on the dock an hour earlier, then of how Paulo had waved away the sandwich trolley at noon. He didn't guess out loud. He pulled out a chair, set a cup of water on the desk and said, "Sit for a minute, no rush." Paulo sat, drank, and after a while said he hadn't eaten since last night. His hands were still unsteady, and neither of them was sure it was only hunger.

qa.q: What did Chidi set on the desk for Paulo?
qa.a: Chidi set a cup of water on the desk.

qa.q: What might Paulo be feeling as he stands by the printer, and what else could explain how he looks?
qa.a: Most likely he feels unwell and a little embarrassed, since he says he is fine yet stays very still with the sheets rattling. Hunger fits, but the shouting match on the dock could also have shaken him.

qa.q: What could Chidi do next if Paulo still looks unwell later?
qa.a: He could make sure Paulo eats something and suggest seeing a doctor or the workplace first aider if it keeps going or worries them. Asking about the dock argument can wait until Paulo is steady.

qa.q: How might Chidi have felt watching Paulo by the printer?
qa.a: Chidi was probably worried but careful, noticing the pale face and rattling sheets, so he offered water and a chair instead of guessing out loud. 🙂

grounding: Illustrates a colleague looking pale and shaky with several possible causes, where checking health and safety comes before judging emotion.

subtopic: Visible reactions with multiple possible causes
passage: Divyansh came out of the manager's cabin at 3:40 and stopped at the door of the audit room. Binita, filing invoices, noticed his lips looked grey and the folder in his hand was trembling. "Was it bad news?" she nearly asked, then stopped herself. Instead she said, "Come, the pantry chairs are free. Let me get you something." He followed slowly. In the pantry she poured him juice and asked whether he felt dizzy or wanted the office first-aid person called. He shook his head, then said he'd had only tea since morning and the meeting had gone on long. He rubbed his palms on his trousers. "And I'm a bit rattled too," he added quietly. Binita nodded and moved her chair so no one walking in would see his face.

qa.q: What had Divyansh had since morning?
qa.a: He had had only tea since morning.

qa.q: What was Binita thinking when she stopped herself from asking about bad news?
qa.a: She saw he was pale and trembling and knew the cause was unclear: it could be hunger, dizziness or upset. She put his wellbeing ahead of guessing at his feelings.

qa.q: What would you advise Divyansh to do later that day?
qa.a: Eat something proper and rest, and check with a doctor if the shakiness keeps going or worries him. If the meeting still bothers him, he could talk it over with a trusted colleague.

qa.q: What might it be like for Divyansh to be asked calmly in the pantry rather than in the open office?
qa.a: He can admit both the hunger and feeling rattled without an audience, which is easier than defending himself in front of others.

grounding: Illustrates a colleague suddenly pale and shaking, where hunger, illness or emotion are all possible and safety is checked first.

passage:
Subject: Checking in after this morning

Hi Naveen,

I wanted to write properly, because at the stand-up I only managed a clumsy "you okay?"

When the director started going through the quarterly numbers, your face went grey and your hands were shaking so much the coffee cup rattled on the table. My first thought, honestly, was that you were scared of the review. I nearly said "relax, it's not that bad."

I'm glad I asked instead whether you'd eaten. When you said nothing since last night, I got the juice from the pantry and sat with you in the small room until your hands stopped trembling.

You said afterwards it was "probably both, the hunger and the nerves." Fair enough. I just didn't want to guess at the feeling before checking you were physically all right. If it keeps happening, please get it checked with a doctor.

Hafsa

qa.q: What did Hafsa bring Naveen from the pantry?
qa.a: Hafsa got the juice from the pantry and sat with Naveen in the small room until the trembling stopped.

qa.q: What was Hafsa feeling on seeing Naveen's hands shaking, and how sure could Hafsa be of the reason?
qa.a: Hafsa was worried and a little unsure: the first reading was that Naveen was scared of the review, but hunger or illness could look the same, so Hafsa checked on Naveen's health first.

qa.q: Which choice worked here, and why?
qa.a: Asking whether Naveen had eaten and staying with Naveen worked, because it dealt with a possible physical cause before anyone judged the mood.

qa.q: How might Naveen have felt if Hafsa had said "relax, it's not that bad"?
qa.a: Naveen might have felt misread and embarrassed, since part of the shaking came from not eating, and would still have been unwell.

grounding: It illustrates a young adult noticing a colleague turn pale and shaky and checking health and safety before deciding it is fear.

passage:
So you asked about the scariest shift I've had at the warehouse. Okay, I'm Kishore, I run the evening dispatch team, and this is the one I still think about.

Shreya takes a phone call near loading bay three. Next minute she's white as chalk, one hand on the rack, knees kind of wobbling. Some of the lads assumed she was furious, because she'd been arguing with a driver earlier.

I didn't know. Could be anger, could be she was going to faint, could be bad news. So I just asked, "Are you hurt? Do you need to sit?" She shook her head, then sat on a pallet anyway. I got water, asked if she wanted anyone called.

Turned out her father had been taken to hospital. Shock, not temper. I called our supervisor to cover her line and booked her a cab. The feelings could wait; getting her safely off the floor couldn't.

qa.q: Where did Shreya take the phone call?
qa.a: She took the phone call near loading bay three.

qa.q: Why did Kishore ask about Shreya's safety before anything else, and what was Kishore feeling?
qa.a: Kishore felt uncertain and concerned, because her paleness and wobbling knees could mean anger, faintness or bad news, so Kishore checked she was not hurt or about to fall before guessing her feelings.

qa.q: How could the other workers handle a moment like this next time?
qa.a: They could stop assuming it is anger, ask a simple question about whether the person is hurt or needs to sit, and help get them somewhere safe.

qa.q: What was it like for Shreya when some of the lads thought she was furious?
qa.a: She had just heard frightening news about her father, so being read as angry would have left her more alone at a moment of shock.

grounding: It shows a young adult seeing a colleague go pale and shaky and putting safety and health ahead of reading the emotion.

subtopic: Visible reactions with multiple possible causes
passage:
I'm Yusuf, and I work the grill next to Akash on weekends. Here's what I saw on Saturday night, for whatever it's worth.

The dinner rush was at its worst. Akash dropped a plate of kebabs, and a few minutes later his face had gone pasty and there was sweat on his lip. His hands shook while he plated.

The head chef shouted, "Nerves, Akash? Toughen up!" Maybe it was nerves. The kitchen was also boiling, and I'd not seen him eat all shift.

I pulled him into the cold store and asked, "Dizzy? Want to sit?" He sat on a crate and said he felt light-headed. Someone brought sweet tea and a roti. After ten minutes his colour came back.

Later he said, "Maybe the heat, maybe the dropped plate. I don't know." I still don't know either. I just knew it wasn't the moment to call it nerves.

qa.q: What did Akash drop during the dinner rush?
qa.a: He dropped a plate of kebabs.

qa.q: How can you tell Akash was unsure about his own feelings, and what did he most likely feel?
qa.a: He said "Maybe the heat, maybe the dropped plate. I don't know," which suggests he felt shaken and light-headed, possibly embarrassed about the plate, though the heat and not eating could explain it just as well.

qa.q: What went wrong in the head chef's response, and what could fix it?
qa.a: The head chef labelled it nerves without asking; a quick check on whether Akash was dizzy, plus water or food and a seat, would have come first.

qa.q: What might Akash have felt if the head chef's "toughen up" had been the only response?
qa.a: Akash might have felt ashamed and kept working while light-headed, which could have made him more unwell in a hot kitchen.

grounding: It illustrates that a colleague suddenly pale and shaking might be feeling fear or be unwell, so the observer checks safety before judging emotion.

passage:
Monday: In the weekly review at the logistics office, Hemant went pale when the regional manager asked about the missing consignment, and his hands shook as he turned the pages. Santosh leaned over and whispered, "Relax, yaar, she won't eat you." Hemant didn't smile.
Wednesday: Santosh found Hemant gripping the photocopier, face grey, sweat on his upper lip. This time Santosh didn't joke. "Hey, are you okay? Do you want to sit? Water? Should I call someone?" Hemant sank into a chair and said he had skipped breakfast and lunch and felt dizzy. Santosh fetched the office first-aider and a packet of biscuits and stayed with him until the colour came back.
The following Monday: Hemant said a doctor had checked him and he now kept food in his drawer. Santosh thought back to that first review. He had been so sure it was nerves. It might have been hunger all along.

qa.q: Who did Santosh fetch on Wednesday along with a packet of biscuits?
qa.a: Santosh fetched the office first-aider.

qa.q: What was Santosh feeling the following Monday when he thought back to the first review?
qa.a: Santosh likely felt uneasy and a little embarrassed that he had been so sure Hemant was nervous, when hunger might have caused the paleness.

qa.q: What went right on Wednesday, and why did it matter?
qa.a: Santosh checked on Hemant's safety first, offered a seat, water or a call, and stayed with him, so a possible health problem was handled before anyone judged emotions.

qa.q: What might Hemant have felt when Santosh joked "she won't eat you" on Monday?
qa.a: Hemant may have felt brushed off and unseen, especially if he was feeling faint rather than scared of the manager.

grounding: Shows that a colleague's sudden paleness or shaking may come from illness or hunger as well as fear, so checking health and safety comes first.
